as_told.title: Chemical analysis of the Giza iron veins

plain: Veins of iron ore running through the bedrock under the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand, are said to be full of precious metals and rare elements. To the man telling it, this is a clue to what the pyramids were really for. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm makes the claim, saying he has chemical analysis data showing these mineral deposits are "permeated with rare earth elements, gold, silver." In a second telling in the same episode he adds electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver, and says the samples hold "everything that you could think of." In a later episode, where he says an alien told him the pyramids' true purpose, he speaks more loosely of "valuable metal deposits." Platinum, named in some versions of the claim, does not appear in his quoted words. All of this rests on Drumm's own account of the analysis, and Michels hosts both conversations.
